references.text: The preceding verse establishes the context regarding punishment when a master strikes his slave and the slave dies immediately.
Concerns slaves as property ('כַסְפּוֹ' - his money/property), explaining the phrase 'for he is his property' in the verse.
Other laws about the treatment of slaves in the same chapter, showing consequences when a master permanently injures his slave.
Refers to Hebrew slaves and their status, relevant for understanding the slavery legislation in the Mosaic Law.
Both verses define the limits of legal liability and punishment in cases of unintentional or unavoidable damage to property.
